title: Using a `distill` vignette on CRAN
description:
The vignette of our package using `distill` renders well on our `pkgdown` [website](https://docs.ropensci.org/nuts/articles/nuts.html). On the [CRAN server](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nuts/vignettes/nuts.html) however there are several issues:

- Links in figure captions
- Labels in plots (e.g. alluvial plot) 

Any clue why?

title: Has anyone used any alternative to Google analytics?
description:
I am intrigued to find that my [Rblog site](https://www.psyctc.org/Rblog/index.html) has grown to 41 posts in three years!  I had thought I was analysing hits with a google tag but clearly had made a mess of that.  I've now fixed that and the "live" view in Google analytics is now showing my visits (!)  I assume that the snapshot takes a day or two build its database before showing analyses.  However, I would really like to move away from Google for analytics, I am successfully moving my web sites to other systems.  I have a sense that someone will have achieved analytics for a distill blog without using Google so I'd really like not  to reinvent the wheel!  

Any suggestions?  I'd particularly appreciate any advice on code necessary.

TIA, 

Chris

title: Journal (site) title is incorrectly prepended to the article title in cititations.
description:
Articles have the journal (site) title prepended unconditionally in the Citation section, i.e. `title = "The R Journal: Some Article"` although it should be correctly `title= "SomeArticle"`, e.g.

For attribution, please cite this work as

Zeng & Breheny, "The R Journal: The biglasso Package: A Memory- and Computation-Efficient Solver
for Lasso Model Fitting with Big Data in R", The R Journal, 2021

BibTeX citation

@article{RJ-2021-001,
  author = {Zeng, Yaohui and Breheny, Patrick},
  title = {The R Journal: The biglasso Package: A Memory- and Computation-Efficient Solver for Lasso Model Fitting with Big Data in R},
  journal = {The R Journal}, [...]
This comes from https://github.com/rstudio/distill/blob/d88adcaacd6b3b4e96e3f2b88449b4b839ddff0a/R/metadata.R#L870-L876 and there seems no way to disable it. I would argue that it is never desirable to have the site title prepended as it is never the title for citation purposes (that's what the `journal` entry is for) and hence I'd call it a bug, but at the very least there should be a way to disable this behavior. Quick fix is to remove the above, but it is also possible that `qualified_title()` is used incorrectly in the citation context.

title: Gallery outdated, remove Quarto pages
description:
Hi there, thanks for all the efforts on the distill packages! 

I just noticed that e.g. "Th MockUp Blog" which is featured as one of a few example pages in the [official gallery here](https://pkgs.rstudio.com/distill/articles/examples.html) is not actually a distill page aynmore but was rebuild as a Quarto page (and, unfortunately, I realized it way too late). 

It would be great if the examples feature only those webpages that actually can serve as distill examples so that the next person doesn't spend too much time not realizing it's a different framework.

title: Various minor accessibility issues
description:
Various minor issues that should be fixed, see e.g. See https://validator.w3.org/nu/?doc=https%3A%2F%2Fjournal.r-project.org%2Farticles%2FRJ-2023-001%2F.

As reported by @hturner in https://github.com/rjournal/rjtools/issues/99#issue-1888055727

title: Space between lines in bulleted lists
description:
Consider the following .Rmd ``` --- title: "bulleted list issues" --- ## Good bullets - one - two - three ## Bad bullets - one blah - two what - three ``` When rendered to html_document the "bad" bullets have a blank line between each bullet point, which is read as "empty line" by screen readers. When rendered to rjtools::rjournal_web_article both sets of bullet points have a blank line between each bullet point. It would be good if the rjtools style did not introduce blank lines in the first case (and authors were encouraged to use this form). The blank lines appear to be due to

tags nested within

  • tags. Originally posted by @ajrgodfrey and @hturner at https://github.com/rjournal/rjtools/issues/102#issue-1888783511

title: Add <hr> for screen reader accessibility
description:
From https://github.com/rjournal/rjtools/issues/92

Currently the title, metadata, article, and appendices are separated using `byline`'s border-top css. It would be nice for accessibility if a (hidden) `<hr>` could be included before each `<d-byline>`  so that screen readers can use it for section navigation.

title: Warning due to deprecation of 'format' argument to 'as.character.POSIXlt()'
description:
The package gives a warning during rendering:

```
Warning message:
In as.character.POSIXt(as.POSIXlt(x), ...) :
  as.character(td, ..) no longer obeys a 'format' argument; use format(td, ..) ?
```

I traced it to 

https://github.com/rstudio/distill/blob/9553c1114ad00a618877e06cab49e93e27d24c41/R/utils.R#L115

I believe `as.character()` should be replaced with `format()`.

title: Embed webpage within Distill blog.
description:
Hello,

I wonder if it is possible to keep the top bar (menu logo), likely the bottom bar (if there is any) and in-between insert an external page. Like for example a contact-me form from netlify.

So far the only way I have found is with this code on a RMD file, that I placed at the bottom.

While this kind of works, it still keep the d-title section (Contact me form) and the iframe require me also to guess the height, which in this case it will not change, but for other cases it might,

My solution also creates a bug when you are knitting in Rstudio, and it opens like millions (more like 9) of new tabs in your default browser (at least on windows 10) pointing to that webpage, which it is annoying, but nothing terrible.

````markdown
---
title: "Contact me form"
description: |
date: 01-01-2023

---


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

```{r}
knitr::include_url("https://contact.rmrubert.eu", height = "750px")
```
````

title: New post does not appear on Distill blog, but is already in the github

I produced a new post on gtsummary package and commited it to github (https://github.com/yuryzablotski/yuzaR-Blog), and pushing worked fine, but my post never appeared on the blog. I even created a new post gtsummary2, which was completely empty and tried to commit and push it to see whether it will appear, but it also did not. I can also see it on the github though, so, the commiting and pushing did work.

Could you please help, or tell me whether there is any other support for Distill possible? There might be some small things I miss, but I tried everything I could think of. 

Kind regards,
Yury

title: Distill article renders to empty page when an (unescaped) @ sign followed by characters is included in the text
description:
Hello, I (may) have encountered an error that a `distill::distill_article` renders to empty/blank page when an @ sign followed by characters (e.g. `@xyz`) is included in the text. I use distill to maintain a blog and noticed that one article of mine where I had an unescaped @ sign in the text was just an empty/blank page. I suspect that this behaviour was introduced after I updated the distill package.

Here is a basic `distill::distill_article` that renders to an empty document when knitting it:

Example 1

``` r
---
title: "Untitled"
description: |
  A new article created using the Distill format.
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: distill::distill_article
---

This distill article is rendered empty when including an @ sign followed by characters:

Example: @xyz
```

![distill_issue](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38919712/175960722-fea11130-9468-40fd-be18-8c728a4aad1e.png)

The following article however does knit properly when the @ sign is escaped by a backslash:

Example 2

``` r
---
title: "Untitled"
description: |
  A new article created using the Distill format.
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: distill::distill_article
---

This distill article is rendered correctly when the @ sign has been escaped:

Example: \@xyz
```

![distill_issue_escaped](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38919712/175961162-059efb6f-198b-40e0-a110-e378b121751a.png)



Traditional RMarkdown Documents do not display this behaviour. Also interesting was that when I used `reprex::reprex_render("distill_test.Rmd")` the distill article of Example 1 with the unescaped @ sign was rendered properly.
I dont really know how, if it is an error or I just have to remember to escape special characters.
I didnt find a post/issue discussing this behaviour. Maybe there are peple who are affected as well.

I uninstalled distill version 1.4 and reinstalled distill version 1.3 and this behaviour disappeared. That means the documents then knitted properly even when there were unescaped @ signs in the text.

title: Figure captions don't work for some text length with `(ref:...`
description:
I'm having a very confusing issue trying to make the "(ref:caption)" syntax work. The code below is a reprex document that describes the issue. 

````
---
title: title
output: 
  distill::distill_article: default
---


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```
Caption works with a 50 character length caption 

(ref:caption1) `r paste0(rep("a", 50), collapse = "")`

```{r , fig.cap = "(ref:caption1)"}
plot(pressure)
```

But not with 51 characters

(ref:caption2) `r paste0(rep("a", 51), collapse = "")`

```{r , fig.cap = "(ref:caption2)"}
plot(pressure)
```


Remove one character from the ref name, and now it works with 51 characters. 


(ref:caption) `r paste0(rep("a", 51), collapse = "")`

```{r , fig.cap = "(ref:caption)"}
plot(pressure)
```


But add another chacater (total of 52 characters) to the caption, and it breaks again.

(ref:kaption) `r paste0(rep("a", 52), collapse = "")`

```{r , fig.cap = "(ref:kaption)"}
plot(pressure)
```


The limit seems to be the number of character in the name and in the caption. 

````
And here's the output: [test.html.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/distill/files/8818093/test.html.zip)


I'm using distill 1.4 and all other packages up-to-date with R 4.2.0


Infuriatingly, I cannot reproduce this behaviour on my institute server, which has R 3.6.3. But installing R 3.6.3 on my laptop does not fix it.

title: Distill website into progressive webapp
description:
Is there a way to convert a static distill website into PWA? I am much into web development but I like the fact that PWAs can be installed into smart phones home screen and can display in full screen plus other features (eg push notifications, etc..). 

I read some online tutorials and understood that we need to add the following to the website root folder before deployment: 
- manifest.json and then link it in the index.html
- serviceworker.js
- app.js to register the service worker
- folder with different icon sizes and splash screen

I followed the instructions from this example https://dev.to/phonerefer/convert-any-static-website-to-pwa-3fkb but could not get it to work. 

Is there a built in way in the distill package to make PWA? or is there a tutorial / github repo with an example that I can follow? 

thank you 


**Update:**
I was able to generate a progressive webapp from distill website by:
- adding service worker, manifest files and icons folder to the root directory (I found this example extremely helpful https://github.com/aladin002dz/PWA) 
- adding this script to the head section of index.html
```
<link rel="manifest" href="manifest.json">
    <script>
        //if browser support service worker
        if('serviceWorker' in navigator) {
          navigator.serviceWorker.register('sw.js');
        };
      </script>
```

The problem is that the script won't persist in index.html if it is regenerated and I will have to manually add it every time. Is there a way to "inject" the script using a function that I can run after I render the site?

title: LaTeX environment support from bookdown
description:
I'm an active `distill` user and am grateful for this nice blogging package. I plan to write more technical math related posts and wanted to use `LaTeX` environments, e.g., `theorem`, `lemma`, `corollary`etc. I've previously asked about #101. I recently revived this discussion on [stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/70557340/theorem-environment-not-rendering-or-cross-referencing-in-distill). I received a [thoughtful solution](https://stackoverflow.com/a/70574003/4687531) where a user made many detailed modifications to the CSS to get it working. As a result I'm intentionally cross-posting and raising this an issue here. Basically, I was a little surprised that `distill` users would need to go to such lengths to make `LaTeX` environments work, given that bookdown has implemented `rmarkdown` versions [here](https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/markdown-extensions-by-bookdown.html) and [here](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/bookdown-markdown.html). I wanted to flag it with the `distill` team to get the official approach to this. Here is the minimal reprex to help understand the issue (from the stackoverflow post above). ```` rmarkdown --- title: "Test Title" description: | Test description author: Test author date: 2021-12-31 output: distill::distill_article: self_contained: false --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE) library(bookdown) ``` # TL;DR; Trying to ensure that theorem environments are working in `distill::distill_article`. # Main theorems With the definitional background established, let's move onto the main theorem of this article. \begin{align} g(X_{n}) &= g(\theta)+g'({\tilde{\theta}})(X_{n}-\theta) \notag \\ \sqrt{n}[g(X_{n})-g(\theta)] &= g'\left({\tilde{\theta}}\right) \sqrt{n}[X_{n}-\theta ] (\#eq:align) \end{align} \begin{theorem}[Delta Method]\label{nthm:deltamethod} g(X_{n}) &= g(\theta)+g'({\tilde{\theta}})(X_{n}-\theta) \notag \\ \sqrt{n}[g(X_{n})-g(\theta)] &= g'\left({\tilde{\theta}}\right) \sqrt{n}[X_{n}-\theta ] (\#eq:align) \end{theorem} We have a labeled and named theorem below, and \@ref(nthm:deltamethod). ::: {.theorem #pythagoras name="Pythagorean theorem"} For a right triangle, if $c$ denotes the length of the hypotenuse and $a$ and $b$ denote the lengths of the other two sides, we have $$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$ ::: We have a labeled and named theorem below, and \@ref(thm:pythagoras). ```` Could anyone please explain how to get these environments from `bookdown` without needing to modify the CSS for each environment? Since `distill` is meant for technical publishing, I assumed there would be a much easier way to get these `bookdown` `LaTeX` environments working directly. I may have missed them due to my lack of understanding.

title: odd behavior with code_folding and echo options
description:
There was odd behavior on this feature in distill (or maybe it's standard and I just struggled with it)... Regardless I am going to put it here so future people and see it.

If you want some sections to fold and others to not (yet **also not echo**, you need to leave the code folding argument empty). If you choose code_folding: True (or any text which is also true), then when you tell a chunk not to fold it will echo. Even if you have knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE). If you choose false, you can't call code_folding on the chunk.

```
---
title: "Localized and global causes"
author:
output:
  distill::distill_article:
    code_folding: 
---
```

```
{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

```
{r norm one, code_folding = T}
ct1 <- rnorm(100)
```
Expected behavior folds.

```
{r norm two, code_folding = F}
ct2 <- rnorm(100)
```
Echo's (this also happens if you add the chunk option echo = F)

```
{r norm three}
ct3 <- rnorm(100)
```
Works nicely when you leave the code_folding argument empty!

_Originally posted by @njudd in https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/160#issuecomment-990873931_

title: Improve search data by refining the article contents metadata
Add `aria-label` to links that use FA icons for accessibility
description: Hi squad, In running my distill site through [WAVE](https://wave.webaim.org/) for accessibility checks, I've run into the "link-with-no-text" warning for the navigation/header links and the sharing links that use FontAwesome icons. We're doing the right thing (according to [the FA accessibility docs](https://wave.webaim.org/)) by using `aria-hidden` for the icons themselves, it's just that the link itself needs an `aria-label` for screen readers. I got around this in the nav bar by using the "bug" in #151 (one man's bug, is another man's workaround), and I think this should be a pretty simple fix for the sharing links, since they already use names ("services") in the YAML. Pseudo-HTML would be something like: ```html ``` https://github.com/rstudio/distill/blob/e53e8340afa386f638464899a66d22d083428b1f/R/collections.R#L672-L676 And it looks like it wouldn't be hard to plug into the existing code as it's set up right now. Let me know if this sounds like it makes sense and/or if you want me to put a PR together. Thanks, Mara

title: Asides push code chunks down in large screen layout
description:
When you have an aside before a code chunk that is longer than your body text, it pushes the code chunk down leaving a large and undesirable amount of whitespace in the article. It would be nice if the aside could go alongside code chunks in the same way it can go alongside body text.

Here's a minimal reproducible example, along with a screenshot.

``````
---
title: "Untitled"
output: distill::distill_article
---

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Vestibulum maximus odio ut libero viverra, varius mattis nisl accumsan.

<aside>

When you have an aside before a code chunk that is longer than your body text, it pushes the code chunk down leaving a large and undesirable amount of whitespace in the article. It would be nice if the aside could go alongside code chunks in the same way it can go alongside body text. This is only an issue with the layout on large screens.

</aside>

```{r}
# An R code chunk
summary(mtcars)
```
``````

![aside](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51542091/139789159-4b320b44-d7cf-4090-a0d0-300ce5b5a7e5.png)

This is only an issue with the layout on large screens, since asides currently go inline with body text on smaller screens. I suspect the reason for the gap is that the asides are still treated as inline on large screens? And the reason for that is related to the reason we don't have floating TOC, because it would conflict with full width figures:

>No current plans to do that (although I agree it's useful which is why we added it to the standard html_document format). The major issue is that we want to allow figures and tables to occupy the full width of the page which would conflict with a TOC in the gutter.

_Originally posted by @jjallaire in https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/16#issuecomment-423292010_

But it would be nice to allow asides to float beside code chunks. I often run into a case where I want to use an aside but can't because of the large gap it creates. Or there are times where I specifically want to place an aside beside a code chunk because they're meant to go together, but the current behaviour prevents that.

title: Support for Submenus
description:
In rmarkdown (at least v2.10+), there is support for submenus (https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/pull/1426) in rmarkdown website. This doesn't seem to work in distill (v1.2) websites. For instance, consider the following `_site.yml`:

```yaml
name: "site"
navbar:
  title: "My Website"
  left:
    - text: "Home"
      href: index.html
    - text: "About"
      href: about.html
      menu:
        - text: "Sub_1"
          href: sub1.html
        - text: "Sub_2"
          menu:
            - text: "Sub_2_below"
              href: sub2.html
```

And the following `index.Rmd`:

```r
---
params:
  root_dir: NULL
title: "Distill Website"
description: |
  Scientific and technical writing, native to the web
output:
  distill::distill_article:
    toc: true
    code_folding: true
---

# Home Page
```

When we render this `Rscript --slave -e "rmarkdown::render('index.Rmd')"`, the index.html has this menu:

![distill_website_menu](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3268173/134940575-9c41eaf1-eca8-4f26-9872-fca5436cd949.png)

The "SUB_2" has no submenu. While if you change the `index.Rmd` to:

```r
---
params:
  root_dir: NULL
title: "Distill Website"
description: |
  Scientific and technical writing, native to the web
---

# Home Page
```

such that the output is no longer a distill article, but a rather rmarkdown article then we get this:

![rmarkdown_website_menu](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3268173/134940871-62268567-93f2-4905-a3b1-8457d7e38a9c.png).

Is it possible to get support for submenus in distill websites?

title: Chunk option `results='asis'` without wrapping the results in `<div>`
description:
Hi, first of all: thanks a lot for bringing together distill and R markdown! I'd like to make a feature request, s. https://community.rstudio.com/t/display-results-of-code-chunk-really-asis-in-distill-not-within-div/115110/1 I would like to use panelsets in distill articles using xaringanExtra (https://github.com/gadenbuie/xaringanExtra#-panelset.) and programmatically create a number of panelsets (for multiple variables of a data frame), the panels filled with the results of multiple code chunks (plots, tables, etc.). Since panelsets work in distill only by using fenced divs, I'd insert these from within the code chunks using cat(), (e.g. cat("::::: {.panelset}", "\n")) and using chunk option results = 'asis' . Please see below some code chunks to illustrate this and the attached .Rmd with a reprex (I had to zip it since Rmd is not an allowed file type). The following code works fine in distill since the fenced divs and all the content for the tabs are integrated in one single code chunk, so there is no problem since all the output is wrapped in one surrounding `
` *results from the code chunk* `
`. ``` ```{r results='asis'} library(xaringanExtra) xaringanExtra::use_panelset() cat("::::: {.panelset}", "\n") cat("::: {.panel}", "\n", "[First Tab]{.panel-name}", "\n") plot(rnorm(50), main = "Plot 1") cat(":::", "\n") cat("::: {.panel}", "\n", "[Second Tab]{.panel-name}", "\n") plot(rnorm(150), main = "Plot 2") cat(":::", "\n") cat(":::::", "\n") ``` If we split the same code into multiple code chunks the panelsets do not work anymore, I guess because the div that opens for starting the panelset does not wrap the entire output, s. the following chunks: ``` ```{r results='asis'} cat("::::: {.panelset}", "\n") cat("::: {.panel}", "\n", "[First Tab]{.panel-name}", "\n") ``` ``` ```{r results='asis'} plot(rnorm(50), main = "Plot 1") cat(":::", "\n") ``` ``` ```{r results='asis'} cat("::: {.panel}", "\n", "[Second Tab]{.panel-name}", "\n") plot(rnorm(150), main = "Plot 2") cat(":::", "\n") cat(":::::", "\n") ``` Since I want to insert panelsets programmatically via loop (with plots and tabs for a varying number of variables from a df), I would need a results='asis' option for distill that really inserts the results as they are, without any wrapping. Hope I could make clear(er) why this would be of help. Thanks a lot! [paneltest.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/distill/files/7234388/paneltest.zip)

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
Cc @cderv

The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

title: The version check for rstudio fails under certain conditions
description:
Specifically, if you try to render the file from a [`targets`](https://github.com/ropensci/targets) pipeline, you get the error

`Distill articles cannot be previewed in this version of RStudio.`

After investigating, it seems that the problem is this line: 
https://github.com/rstudio/distill/blob/33f858a0e56cd083d55d8ff8df2ed7eecd27372a/R/rstudio.R#L43

The environment variable "RSTUDIO_VERSION" does not exist in my version of RStudio (Windows; 1.4.1725). `targets` uses `callr`, so the rstudioapi is not available, but the "RSTUDIO" environment variable still exists. Since the "RSTUDIO_VERSION" does not exist, it uses the default value which fails the check. I cannot find in the RStudio docs if this variable is no longer set.

I can't think of how to make a reprex for this, but as a way to reproduce you can pull the [targets minimal example repo](https://github.com/wlandau/targets-minimal) and change the Rmd to use distill. Then call `targets::tar_make()`.

As a workaround (for anyone else who finds this), I posed a solution [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68888905/cannot-render-distill-article-in-a-targets-pipeline/68991226#68991226), which is just to define the environment variable at the top of the Rmd file (e.g., `Sys.setenv("RSTUDIO_VERSION" = '1.4.1725')`).

title: Add a "last updated" field or revision history to blog posts
description:
# Summary
I'd like to suggest a feature, that would allow to keep the original publication date but provide means to document changes to posts visible to the reader. Blog authors could also choose to sort the posts in listings according to original publication date or by the "last updated" date.

# Details and example
In the rendered blog post, the "last updated" date would be shown e.g. next to the publication date or at the beginning of the article.
_**Taking the idea further**_, there could be a revision history to make changes transparent/visible to the readers. This revision history would be collapsed by default below the publication date, but can be extended to show all changes.

Here's an example of what I'm suggesting:.

In the YAML header an author could add a date and a string indicating what was added, e.g.

```
date: 2021-08-20   <-- this is the original publication date
updates:
  - date: 2021-08-22
    comment: |
      There was an error in the code creating Fig. 2 (thank's to the reader pointing this out). 
      Now comes a long explanation, what went wrong, that is interesting to share, 
      but would not fit in the blog-text, as it is not relevant for someone who just wants
      to read the current version of the post...
  - date: 2022-05-01
    comment: Re-ran the code with the latest data, however this doesn't change the final result much.

```

In the `_site.yml` there could be an option to choose, whether the blog sorts the posts according to the original date or the "last updated" date.

I'm not sure if this is a need felt by many users, but I still hope, you'll consider it.

You can close this. 🙂

output:

description:

- {distill} v1.2
- R 4.0.5

create_post("An example post", author = "Felipe Ortega")

---
title: "An example post"

title: Guidance for version controlling files
description:
I greatly appreciate how easy it is to get a nice-looking, well-functioning blog working with this package. The one thing I am a bit confused about regarding the writing and publishing workflow is what files I should place under version control. Following the workflow of rendering posts individually, then then running `rmarkdown::render_site()` to render the whole site, leads to a lot of duplication of files in the `_posts/` and `_site/` directories, and some files (like the html file) that are not complete duplicates but largely redundant. In most of the Distill blogs on Github, and in the various tutorials online, users seem to be committing all of these files, including the site libraries which get duplicated in each post in `_posts/` and start to add up to a lot of files for many posts. I'm not sure if this is purely because it's easier to `git add` everything or if there is a reason to track the content in `_posts/` and `_site/` to ensure reproducibility or something. I'm very interested to know if the creators can give any guidance about whether it is a good idea to

1. Track everything, including the site library, figure, and html files in _posts/ directory that are produced by rendering the the R-markdown files, even if you're also tracking all of _site
2. Just track the R markdown files and the _site/ folder
3. Something else.

I think it could be helpful if the documentation added a recommendation about how to most effectively use version control in the Creating a Blog or Blog Post Workflow pages. I understand there may not be a one-size-fits-all answer here, in which case perhaps a note clarifying the relationship of the various files would help confused users like me make a good decision for them.

I have quite a lot of them in my [Blogdown site](https://plussixoneblog.com/). They all live in the `content/posts/` folder. There is usually an `.Rmd` file and a matching `.html` file in that folder (some older posts are just `.md` from when I migrated from wordpress to blogdown).

Is there a way to get all of those old posts to work in Distill without having to update the `YAML` and re-render them? Most of the posts are pretty old and broken so re-rendering won't work but I'd still like to keep them for posterity if possible.

An example post is [here](https://github.com/jimmyday12/plussixoneblog/blob/main/content/post/2020-08-03-new-fitzroy-functions.en.Rmd).

I've tried simply copying and pasting the files (both `Rmd` and `html`) over to the `_posts/` folder and then using `rmarkdown::render_site` to preview things but none of the posts appear on the home page. New posts I add with `distill::create_post` do appear on the home page.

I also tried using `distill::import_post` but kept getting errors. Specifically, I tried the below and received this error.

```
distill::import_post("https://plussixoneblog.com/post/my-elo-rating-system-explained/")
Importing https://plussixoneblog.com/post/my-elo-rating-system-explained/...
This article does not have a creative commons license. Import anyway? [Y/n]: Y
Error in if (dir_exists(article_dir) && !overwrite) { :

```

Any advice would be appreciated and let me know if this is not the best place to ask.

Thanks

title: df_print option is ignored in Distill YAML header
description:
Right now, any attempt to set the `df_print` option in YAML is ignored when rendering articles or posts.

As far as I can tell, this option is not [passed to `render_context()`](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/1707d0b5189e3f12caf16a6cd53391f5be2b2f08/R/knit_print.R) so R Markdown isn't able to pick it up when knitting the document. This seems inconsistent with most other R Markdown output formats.

### Workaround

Current workaround is as follows: add a chunk near the top of your Rmd file with the following, assuming you want `df_print: kable`.

```r
library(knitr)
# define a method for objects of the class data.frame
knit_print.data.frame = function(x, ...) {
  res = paste(c('', '', kable(x, 'html'), ''), collapse = '\n')
  asis_output(res)
}
# register the method
registerS3method("knit_print", "data.frame", knit_print.data.frame)
```

Then your Distill articles will knit as if they were another format with `df_print: kable` in the header. Source for this fix is the [knitr vignette on custom print methods](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/knitr/vignettes/knit_print.html).

title: yaml documentation: _site.yml vs yaml in .Rmd
description:
Hi distill developers!  Thank you so much for your work on this package, I am so thankful for its existence!  

One thing that I struggled with in getting started with distill, and still struggle a bit with, is understanding all the options for the yaml in distill, and furthermore, understanding how the options may be used in an individual `.Rmd` for a blog post vs the `_site.yml`.  In addition, I am also unclear as to whether this means I should read Rmarkdown documentation more generally or focus on distill documentation. 

There is a lot of great content regarding the yaml throughout the distill documentation, which has helped me tremendously, and I thank you for that! - Is this option specific to distill or is it a more general Rmarkdown yaml option? (Maybe that could help with understanding which documentation to read for futher help.)
- Should this option be used in `_site.yml`, the yaml of a `.Rmd`, or possibly both?  
- If possibly both, does one option override the other? Do they serve the same purpose or a different purpose?

For example, I have `base_url` in both my `_site.yml` and the yaml of my `.Rmd`s.  I think this would be the answers to the above questions: 
- the `base_url` is a yaml option specific to distill
- the `base_url` can be specified in either the `_site.yml` or the yaml of a `.Rmd`
- when specified, it serves different purposes. `_site.yml` is for an RSS feed, `.Rmd` is for social media posts

Is this correct?  

Thank you for taking the time to read this verbose issue! Please let me know if I can further clarify anything.

title: Pandoc-style R code fences do not get downlit syntax highlighting
description:
Hi,

I was playing around some more and I noticed that if you use pandoc-style code fences but mark them as `R` code, then they do not get the same syntax hightlighting as R Markdown `R` code chunks. I suppose this makes sense since `downlit` is only used on an R Markdown code chunk that has the `"R"` engine (`if (downlit && options$engine == "R")`), and any code contained in code fences are handed off to pandoc for syntax highlighting.

Seems like this could be a bit tricky to handle, perhaps using a regex, but not impossible. Perhaps the recommendation should just be to use proper R Markdown chunks and set `eval = FALSE` to get consistent highlighting for documents using `downlit` (@hadley thoughts?).

Just thought I would share this observation, feel free to close the issue if you think it's not worth acting on. This issue can at least serve as a reminder of why this may crop up in some cases.

In the example below, chunk 1 has default pandoc highlighting, while chunk 2 and 3 are formatted the same using `downlit`.
````
---
title: "My Website"
description: |
  Welcome to the website. I hope you enjoy it!
site: distill::distill_website
---

```r
1 + 2
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
1 + 2
```

```{r}
1 + 2
```
````

I'm not sure if this issue belongs here or in crosstalk, but I haven't had the same issue when using crosstalk filters with other R Markdown templates.

Here are two sample Rmds that exhibit the behavior. The first is the default distill output:

````

title: Shiny dashboards layout mangled by distill
description: Unfortunately, shiny dashboards are confined to the article box in distill and then rearranged by shiny to make them fit that box "well". When using ctrl & +, this scales all content equally, so the problematic formatting remains. See https://www.jbarg.net/incident_dashboard for an example. Here is the original deployment with a much more sensible formatting: https://julianbarg.shinyapps.io/incident_dashboard/ .The element on the left side uses the shiny sidepanel feature, which a lot of people rely on to build their dashboards, so certainly this kind of formatting would be the most frequent one we encounter when integrating a shiny dashboard into distill. Here is the source code for that article: https://github.com/julianbarg/jules_net/blob/main/incident_dashboard.Rmd . It pretty much just consists of the standard shiny dashboard html snippet: ```<iframe height="800" width="100%" frameborder="no" src="https://julianbarg.shinyapps.io/incident_dashboard/"> </iframe>```.

title: Create others listings like _posts
description:
Hi, thank you for this package. I've been using a homemade framework based on [rmarkdown driven development](https://emilyriederer.netlify.app/post/rmarkdown-driven-development/) using  `rmarkdown::render_site()` but this simplify my whole workflow !

# Problem

In the website i'm working on, I want to organize posts in different folders, for example:

- `applications` containing all shiny apps related posts,
- `analysis` containing all data analysis reports posts,
- ...

On the website this would translate to one navbar link for each directory, each one of them would be a listing of the corresponding category.

# What I tried

Create a directory for each category:
```
- _applications/
  - sample_post_1/
    - sample_post_1.Rmd
- _analysis/
  - sample_post_2/
    - sample_post_2.Rmd
- site.yml
- index.Rmd
- applications.Rmd
- analysis.Rmd
```

`application.Rmd` and `analysis.Rmd` contains custom listings like below:

```
---
title: "Applications"
listing: applications
---
```

My `site.yml` contains the following:

```
...
  right:
    - text: "Home"
      href: index.html
    - text: "Applications"
      href: applications.html
    - text: "Analysis"
      href: analysis.html
...
```

# Error

When I build the website I get the following error:

```
Rendering: ./applications.Rmd
Erreur : The collection 'applications' does not have an article listing.
(try running render_site() to generate the listing)

Exited with status 1.
```

# Workaround

I was able to make this work by putting all posts in `_posts` directory and create manual listing like this:

```
- _posts/
  - sample_post_1/
    - sample_post_1.Rmd
  - sample_post_2/
    - sample_post_2.Rmd
```

in `applications.Rmd`

```
---
title: "Applications"
listing: 
  posts:
    - sample_post_1
---
```

The problem with that is that the manual list will be hard to maintain when a lot of `.Rmd` files exist in the `_posts` directory.

# Question

**Is there a way to create new directories that works like `_posts` directory works ?**

title: Add argument "format" to "distill::article" in order to use distill format in pkgdown articles
description:
I would like to use pkgdown to build an html article with the (very nice) distill format. 

As per the documentation of `pkgdown::build_articles`, "By default, pkgdown builds all articles with rmarkdown::html_document() by setting the template parameter." As suggested I have tried to override this by adding

```
pkgdown:
  as_is: true
```

to the yaml metadata of the default distill vignette, leading to the following minimal vignette:

````r
---
title: "Untitled"
description: |
  A new article created using the Distill format.
author:
  - name: Nora Jones 
    url: https://example.com/norajones
    affiliation: Spacely Sprockets
    affiliation_url: https://example.com/spacelysprokets
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: distill::distill_article
pkgdown:
  as_is: true
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

Distill is a publication format for scientific and technical writing, native to the web. 

Learn more about using Distill for R Markdown at <https://rstudio.github.io/distill>.
````

When running `pkgdown::build_articles` I get the following error:

```r
> pkgdown::build_articles()
-- Building articles ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reading 'vignettes/test-distill-vignette.Rmd'
-- RMarkdown error --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Error in html_document_base(smart = smart, self_contained = self_contained,  : 
  formal argument "template" matched by multiple actual arguments
```

This is consistent with the documentation of pkgdown::build_articles: the output_format  "must accept template, theme, and self_contained in order to work with pkgdown", and it is not the case for `distill::article` which forces `format="default"`. 

My understanding is that adding an argument `format` to `distill::article` would address this issue.

```r
> packageVersion("distill")
[1] ‘1.1’
```

title: Upgrade a11y highlighter
description:
+ `#f7f7f8` (.at) flagged as low contrast

+ `#D91E18` "cn" is a bit too bright too- maybe switch to `#A1024A`. In downlit:
    ```
    constant <- c(
        "NA", "Inf", "NaN", "TRUE", "FALSE",
        "NA_integer_", "NA_real_", "NA_character_", "NA_complex_"
     )
    ```

+ consider pulling the colours "40%" towards a fixed chroma

+ remove bolds


Code from @hadley for calculating contrast ratios:
```
rel_l <- function(x) {
  scale <- function(x) {
    ifelse(x <= 0.03928, x / 12.92, ((x + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
  }
  rgb <- farver::decode_colour(x) / 255
  0.2126 * scale(rgb[, 1]) + 0.7152 * scale(rgb[, 2]) + 0.0722 * scale(rgb[, 3])
}
contrast_ratio <- function(x, y) {
  x_l <- rel_l(x)
  y_l <- rel_l(y)
  (pmax(x_l, y_l) + 0.05) / (pmin(x_l, y_l) + 0.05)
}
```

Also gist from @hadley for parsing the theme into CSS:
https://gist.github.com/hadley/f53b6e92df20994fdabe6562d284728a

Similar to: enabled by bootstrap.  - Alternate strategy: if repository\_url present in \_site.yml, allow users to enable buttons to edit or view source Rmd for each article, as is possible in blogdown/Hugo () and bookdown::gitbook () - See also: [rhub blog](https://blog.r-hub.io/2020/09/03/keep.source/) 10. More flexible handling of per-article **table of contents**; i.e., option for fixed position TOC in the left-hand gutter, doesn't need to be sticky [[issue](https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/16)]; this [Distill article](https://distill.pub/2020/communicating-with-interactive-articles/) has a good example: 11. **Code-folding** doesn't work natively [[issue](https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/160), [issue](https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/77)] - Package creating to do this for bookdown and distill: [codefolder](https://github.com/ijlyttle/codefolder) - [Stack overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/a/45501553) - [Details CSS](https://github.com/mrworthington/mrworthington.github.io/blob/master/styles.css#L106-L154) to create expandable sections - this breaks **gutter text** and **\** may also minorly affect other CSS components 12. Consider tabbed panels that allow code/figures [[issue](https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/11)] 13. Built-in **copy to clipboard** for code chunks like with pkgdown [[issue](https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/156), [issue](https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/89)] - note: actually less sure about this feature since echo = FALSE is the default, but it comes up frequently as a feature request across our website-making tools 14. Look into ways to scaffold custom styles, add more on Distill CSS to documentation. Related issues: - - - -

title: Pagination for post listing?
description:
This is mostly blog thing.

Over time, as you accumulate posts the listing can get quite long and it begins to affect the homepage load time, especially if there are cover images for each post. Image optimisation can mitigate it to a degree, but it's really an uphill battle against something that will inevitably become a problem the more you post.

Pagination would be a nice to have to deal with this. I know it is possible to say exactly which posts appear on the page but it would be good to be able to say 'the latest n' where n is a number of my choosing. Combine that with an archive listing perhaps?.  

Another option would be full pagination with n posts per page divided over as many necessary pages as necessary.

The tag filtering might get a bit tricky.

title: Support for code folding
description:
Currently, `distill` doesn't support native cold-folding as implemented by `RMarkdown` YAML:

Thus, the below doesn't work.

````
---
output:
  html_document:
    code_folding: show
---
```{r}
1
```
```{r, class.source='fold-hide'}
2
```
````

# Alternatives

### `codefolder` via JS

Ian Lyttle has created a small R package to enable code folding [here](https://github.com/ijlyttle/codefolder)  
  - Based off this [StackOverflow post](https://stackoverflow.com/a/45501553)

### `<details>` via CSS

title: HTML tables get modified by `distill`
description:
Cross-posting this from `gt` Issue #643 [here](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/643).

---
The `distill` RMarkdown format appears to override portions of `gt` tables. This leads to double "plotting" of header borders, and adds row dividers even if they've been excluded via `tab_options()`.

This also appears to occur with [`kableExtra`](https://github.com/haozhu233/kableExtra/issues/279) and further documented [here](https://haozhu233.github.io/kableExtra/using_kableExtra_in_radix.html).

My assumption is that there is a `boostrap` or `CSS` conflict. If it's more appropriate to reference this in the `distill` repo let me know!

```r
library(gt)

mtcars %>% 
  head() %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_spanner(
    2:5,
    label = "Spanner"
  ) %>% 
  tab_options(
    table_body.hlines.color = "white",
    column_labels.border.bottom.width = px(3),
    column_labels.border.bottom.color = "black",
    table.border.top.color = "white",
    table.border.top.width = px(3),
    table.border.bottom.color = "black",
    table.border.bottom.width = px(3)
  )
```

title: Project skeleton/yml source for metadata
description:
_or:_ how to get rid of Nora Jones and Spacely Sprockets...

New user of distill here.

- I used the RStudio "New RMarkdown" procedure to create a new article in my distill project. I was dismayed to find that none of the YAML options I had already used in my existing index.Rmd (eg author) were used in the new article
- I realised that this is because it just uses the default skeleton from the package `inst` directory - this process would not be aware of any settings internal to the current project
- So then I thought, I'll use a distill script to create a new article. That should be able to read off environment settings such as author name. But no. There is no `distill::create_article()` script. Only create_post(). This is a terminological confusion for newbies, as the RStudio menu procedure refers to 'articles' not 'posts'. And the distill website 'Basics' page also refers to articles not posts. There is also the function `distill::distill_article()` that uses this terminology
- The example given on the distill website (`rmarkdown::draft("article.Rmd", "distill_article", package = "distill")`) is helpful because you can pass `edit = TRUE` to it. However I was once again dismayed that upon using `edit = TRUE` for a second time, the skeleton was unchanged from the original default: the changes I had made in my first usage of edit were not persistent
- It's not clear to me how to set up persistent default metadata options or a default template for new articles within the current project
- It would be great if there were a project file, like `_site.yml`, where these metadata options could be set, if desired, so that `distill::create_post()` would read them in when creating a new article within the current project
- The documentation says `#' @param author Post author. Automatically drawn from previous post if not provided.` but this did not work for me (I had already set up my name as metadata in my initial index.Rmd but when creating a new post (article) the author name appeared as "Unknown"
- It would also be good I think if there was a function `distill::create_article()`, either as an alias to `create_post()` or with its own slightly different defaults (I'm assuming here that articles within a technical writing website are often going to be set up quite differently to posts within a blog site. But I accept that this is a matter of personal preference.)

Thanks!

My hunch is that this the following CSS never gets disabled on render, as it probably should:

```
<style type="text/css">
  /* Hide doc at startup (prevent jankiness while JS renders/transforms) */
  body {

  }

```

Manually deleting this section from the `index.html` lets Safari show the website, though the css (fonts) are mucked up.

on_load_complete();
```

title: Using # for section titles with --base-header-level=2 instead of using ## ?
description:
As many other HTML templates, radix is using `h1` for the title of the article and `h2` for the different sections.

Following this, the corresponding expected markdown is something like:

```
---
title: "title of the article"
---

## Section 1

text

## Section 2

### Sub-section 2.1

text
```

This use of `h2` for level-1 section headers is due to a historical limit of HTML (with not proper `<title>` or equivalent in the `<body>`).

However, for LaTeX or Word output, it is expected to use `#` for the level-1 section headers, which is **semantically** more correct.

One interest of markdown is the possibility to transform it into different outputs. However, currently, the markup of level-1 sections (`##` expected for HTML/radix vs `#` for LaTeX/Word output) is a problem.

Ideally, the markup in the markdown should not depend on the type of output.

A possibility could be for radix articles to expect the following markdown:

```
---
title: "title of the article"
---

# Section 1

text

# Section 2

## Sub-section 2.1

text
```

and to use the pandoc option `--base-header-level=2` to properly transform `#` into `<h2>` keeping the same semantic of `#` between HTML, LaTeX and Word, while having the appropriate HTML markup.

As Radix is still in the development phase, would it be an appropriate time to discuss the relevance of such behaviour?

title: navbar icon and text not working together
description:
In navbars, one can only use text or icon to create an item, but not both. depending on the context, either the icon or the text will "win". 

* for top-level items, only the icon is considered
* for top-level menu headers, only the text is considered 
* for menu items, only the icon is considered

YAML example: 

```
navbar:
  left:
    - text: "info"                           # text is disregarded
      icon: fa-list-alt                      # icon is considered
      href: index.html
    - text: "Preprocessing"                  # text is considered
      icon: fa-hourglass-half                # icon is disregarded
      menu:
        - text: "Preprocessing pipeline"     # text is disregarded
          icon: fa-hourglass-half            # icon is considered
          href: pre_pipeline.html
```

title: migrate to pandoc-citeproc for references
description:
as I understand, *most* other rmarkdown formats support citations via pandoc-citeproc, which has a bunch of advantages:

- established syntax/functionality
- *pretty* good bibtex parser (no problems such as in #24)
- arbitrary styles via the CSL standard (as also raised in #36)

@jjallaire mentioned in #24 that radix currently uses distill, which in turn uses some js bibtex parser, which might be hard to disentangle.

I'm wondering whether it might be possible/might make sense to just ignore that part of distill, and do the usual rmarkdown pandoc-citeproc dance.

I'm in no position to say whether this would sit well with the rest of distill (does it do any additional black magic to citations?).
I guess the CSS would have to change a bit to retain the hover-citations (which are great).

If so, I might try to take a whack at this.

I just think it'd be a great benefit to rmarkdown users if all rmarkdown formats behave roughly the same when it comes to these features wrapped from pandoc.

title: Figures can not have width smaller than chunk layout
description:
When an image is put in a code chunk and a width smaller than the layout width is selected (either through fig.width or out.width), the final image is scaled up to take the full width of the layout. In the case of plots created by code this means the plot is created with the intented size and then scaled up - making fonts larger than intended and making the image pixelated. 

I have tested this with ggplot2::ggplot and knitr::include_graphics and the issue occurs in both - makes it very hard to include small images or plots with large height/width ratios.

title: support different reference section styling
description:
Many scholarly journals have very specific requirements for how to format citations in the reference section, such as the Vancouver style, etc, etc. The [Citation Styling Language](https://citationstyles.org/) (CSL) is a format to take care of that formatting, and has a few thousand styles used by journals. BibTeX has such functionality too, e.g. `natlib`, etc.

Please add support for this and guidance at https://rstudio.github.io/radix/citations.html#citing-other-works on how to use it.

Maybe [citation.js](https://citation.js.org/) can be of help.

title: processing protection of bibtex titles is displayed incorrectly
description:
First of all thanks for that great format!

I have some minor issue: some bibtex generator (in my case Zotero with better bibtex) try to protect titles against further processing from biblatex with double curly brackets. That is in complience with biblatex see [BibTex FAQ Question 5](http://ctan.math.illinois.edu/biblio/bibtex/contrib/doc/btxFAQ.pdf). However radix displays these:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29424409/45927171-3b0ee480-bf2f-11e8-8a16-27ca5be69432.png)

Example Bibtex file:

```
@article{HildebrandtExploringFactorModel2016,
  title = {Exploring {{Factor Model Parameters}} across {{Continuous Variables}} with {{Local Structural Equation Models}}},
  volume = {51},
  issn = {0027-3171, 1532-7906},
  doi = {10.1080/00273171.2016.1142856},
  language = {en},
  number = {2-3},
  journal = {Multivariate Behavioral Research},
  author = {Hildebrandt, Andrea and L\"udtke, Oliver and Robitzsch, Alexander and Sommer, Christopher and Wilhelm, Oliver},
  month = may,
  year = {2016},
  pages = {257-258}
}
```

This works flawless with all other markdown formats I've been using.

If you need further information to reproduce this, please let me know.

title: problem for navbar text without href
description:
Hi,

Congrats on the CRAN release - I have been lurking, using this for a while; IMHO this is super-useful and looks great!

Using the new CRAN version, I get a weird problem when I put in a navbar `text` item without a corresponding `href` item. My use case is wanting to have headers and `---` separators in the navbar menu.

If I do something like this:

```
navbar:
  right:
    - text: "Home"
      href: index.html
    - text: "About"
      href: about.html
      menu: 
      - text: "header"
      - text: "Thing 1"
        href: index.html
      - text: "Thing 2"
        href: index.html
```

Then the html does not show up properly in the RStudio Preview window, nor at Github pages. However, it does show up locally if I open using a browser.

If I open the JavaScript console from the RStudio Preview window (or from GH pages), it gives me this error:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'replace' of undefined
    at HTMLAnchorElement.<anonymous> (index.html:1182)
    at Function.each (jquery.min.js:2)
    at m.fn.init.each (jquery.min.js:2)
    at init_common (index.html:1181)
    at init_distill (index.html:875)
    at yh (webcomponents.js:234)

Here are links to the working [site](https://ijlyttle.github.io/radixtest/) and [repository](https://github.com/ijlyttle/radixtest).

title: Figure captions
description:
Thanks for the great publication format!

Currently, figures created in an R code chunk do not get a figure number in the caption, nor is the caption text formatted (unlike when an alternative text is provided in e.g. `![Figure from https://example.com](heatmap.png)`). Would it be possible to 1. output figure numbers into figure captions, and 2. format figure captions similar to how captions to `![Figure from https://example.com](heatmap.png)` images are formatted?

description:
Perhaps an enhancement could be to add support for a search feature via google or duckduck go that can be updated like the rss feed. This would add more general search capability past the tag filters.

Example: _search.html

```
> <form method="get" action="https://duckduckgo.com/">
> 	  <label for="search-field" class="show-for-sr">Search the site</label>
> 	  <input type="search" name="q" maxlength="255" placeholder="Search the site" id="search-field">
> 	  <input type="hidden" name="sites" value="https://my_website.com/"/>
> 	  <input type="hidden" name="k7" value="#faf8f8"/>
> 	  <input type="hidden" name="kj" value="#b33"/>
> 	  <input type="hidden" name="ky" value="#fafafa"/>
> 	  <input type="hidden" name="kx" value="b"/>

title: cross-referencing figures and tables
description:
This issue is a question for which I was unsure whether to place it here, on Stack Overflow or in the R Studio Community forum. I decided to place it here and appreciate to be informed if that is inappropriate, in which case I would move it the appropriate place.

The cross-referencing capabilities for equations, tables and figures that the ```bookdown``` package adds to the conventional Pandoc Markdown has become my favourite feature. For smaller reports, I exclusively use the `html_document2` and `pdf_document2` output formats.

I have played around with the `radix` package and have joy using it and exploring the great new capabilities. But, I am missing the ability to use the ```\@ref(label)``` feature with the figure label being, e.g. `fig:foo`, as described in this section of the `bookdown` book: https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/figures.html

Is it planned to add this feature to the `radix` package in the future? Is there another way that I could implement it myself?
